system_prompt: You design levels for a small tower-defense game (Cannons) and test your own design hypotheses by simulation before trusting them. Be specific and falsifiable: state a hypothesis, then build ONE level designed to be a sharp test of it (not a generic level). Ground hypotheses in the real rules below — never invent a mechanic that isn't stated there, no matter how plausible it sounds.
user_prompt:
GAME RULES — authoritative, matches sim/engine.py and the real Unity game
exactly. Do not assume any mechanic beyond what's stated here: if a field
below isn't described as affecting something, it has NO effect on that thing.
If you're about to justify a hypothesis by what a pirate's `tipo` value does
mechanically, stop — re-read this block first.

- Grid: 5 columns (0-4). At most one cannon per column.
- Pirate fields: column, hp, tipo, position (0, 1, or 2; advancing to
  position 3 ends the game in a loss for whoever is at that position).
- `tipo` (1, 2, 3, or 4) is COSMETIC ONLY — which sprite/skin is used.
  Tipo 1-3 = normal pirates, all three IDENTICAL in stats and behavior.
  Tipo 4 just marks "this is the level's last pirate" (used for music/UI in
  the real game). No tipo value changes damage taken, damage dealt, whether a
  pirate can be targeted, or blocking. A tipo-3 pirate with HP 1 dies to one
  base-damage hit exactly like a tipo-1 pirate with HP 1 — there is no
  immunity, no armor, no special resistance tied to tipo, ever.
- Damage: a placed cannon has `damage` (1 base; merging adds the absorbed
  cannon's damage). Each round, a column's cannon (if any) hits ONLY the
  single most-advanced pirate in that column (highest `position`) — every
  other pirate in that column is untouched that round, regardless of tipo.
- Blocking: because only the most-advanced pirate in a column is ever hit, a
  pirate standing behind another pirate in the same column can't be damaged
  until the one in front dies. This is purely a POSITION effect — whichever
  pirate currently has the highest `position` in that column blocks the
  others behind it. It has nothing to do with tipo; a tipo-1 pirate in front
  blocks exactly as hard as a tipo-3 or tipo-4 pirate in front would.
- Round order (engine.py: apply_action -> shoot_phase -> next_round): player
  places/moves one cannon -> shoot phase (as above) -> pirates advance one
  position -> next wave spawns.
- Merge: placing a cannon onto an already-occupied column absorbs the
  resident cannon's damage (new damage = own + resident's) and destroys the
  resident.
- Loss: any pirate reaching position 3 ends the game immediately.
- Win: all filas (waves) have been spawned AND no pirates remain alive.

Ground every hypothesis in these rules (or in what sim/engine.py's source
actually does, if you have reason to check it) — never invent behavior for a
field this block doesn't say affects anything.


Level JSON schema (must match exactly):
{
  "levelNumber": <int>,
  "password": "<1 uppercase letter + 4 digits, e.g. Q1234>",
  "isHard": <bool>,
  "filas": [
    {"cuadros": [{"index": <0-4>, "tipo": <1-4>, "hp": <1-10>}, ...]},
    ...
  ]
}
Each "fila" is one wave/round. "cuadros" may be an empty list (a breathing-room
round with no pirates). "index" is the column (0=right .. 4=left). "tipo" 1-3
are visually-different normal pirates (same difficulty), 4 marks the last
pirate of the level (use it exactly once, on the final fila that has any
pirates). Max 5 cuadros per fila (one per column, no two pirates share a
column+round).


Confirmed rules so far from previous cycles:
- **Hypothesis:**  
A final pirate (tipo 4) with HP = k can be eliminated without any merges if there are at least k consecutive empty filas directly above it in the same column, because the cannon’s base damage = 1 is applied on every wave, including empty ones. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
The cannon can fire at only one column per wave (i.e., each wave delivers a single point of damage to a single chosen column). Consequently, a level that places two or more pirates with total HP > (number of filas) in different columns becomes unwinnable without merges, even though each column individually would receive enough damage if the cannon could hit all columns simultaneously. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
A final pirate (tipo 4) does **not** receive the cannon’s base damage = 1 during empty filas that occur before its own fila; it can only be damaged starting from its own wave. Consequently, a level that places a final pirate with HP > 1 after only empty filas should be unwinnable without performing a merge. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
If, in any single column, the sum of the HP of all pirates from the first (topmost) pirate in that column down to the final fila exceeds the number of filas spanned by that segment (i.e., the count of rows from that first pirate to the last fila inclusive), then the level cannot be cleared without performing at least one merge, even when each individual pirate’s HP is low enough to be killable on its own. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
If a column contains pirates whose HP values are not non‑increasing (i.e., a lower pirate has higher HP than a pirate above it), the level can be unwinnable without any merges even when each pirate’s HP does not exceed the number of filas remaining from its own fila to the final fila. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis**  
When a pirate that blocks the line of fire is killed in a wave, the cannon’s damage continues in that same wave to affect the next pirate in the same column (i.e., damage can pass through a killed blocker within the same wave). => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis**  
A pirate of tipo 2 cannot be eliminated using only the cannon’s base damage = 1, even when there are enough waves (filas) to deal its total HP; it requires at least one merge unless its HP ≤ 2. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis**  
A pirate (of tipo 1, 2, or 4) with HP = k cannot be eliminated without performing a merge if the number of remaining filas from the wave in which it first appears (including that wave) is fewer than k, since the cannon can inflict at most one point of damage to its column per wave. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
A pirate of type 1, 2, or 4 does **not** receive any cannon damage during empty filas that occur before the wave in which it first appears; its HP can only be reduced starting from its own fila onward. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-25)
- **Hypothesis:**  
If, in a single column, the sum of the HP of all pirates from the first pirate in that column down to the final fila equals the number of filas spanned by that segment, the level can be cleared without performing any merges. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-26)
- **Hypothesis:**  
If two or more pirates occupy the same fila (row) in different columns, they block each other’s line of fire – the cannon cannot target any column that contains a pirate while another pirate in the same fila is still alive. Consequently, a level that has any fila with multiple alive pirates should be unwinnable without performing merges. => confirmed NOT winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-26)
- **Hypothesis:**  
Merges are restricted to pirates that occupy the same column (i.e., they must be vertically adjacent). A merge between two pirates that are only sharing the same fila but are in different columns is not permitted. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-26)
- **Hypothesis**  
A cannon can fire multiple times within a single wave: after dealing damage (and possibly killing) a pirate in one column, you may immediately fire again at a different column in the same wave, provided the first column’s pirate is dead. If this is false, a level that places two 1‑HP pirates in the same fila but different columns will be unwinnable without a merge. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-26)
- The cannon’s damage increase from a merge is applied instantly – the merged‑damage cannon can deal the combined damage in the same wave’s shooting phase. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-26)
- **Hypothesis:**  
Merges performed on a column during rows that contain no pirates increase the cannon’s damage permanently, so a cannon can be “pre‑charged” in empty rows and later kill a high‑HP pirate without any additional merges after the pirate appears. => confirmed winnable by test level. (confidence 0.50, 2026-08-26)

Seed hypotheses worth stress-testing (human-authored guesses, not verified by
your own play — confirm, refine, or overturn them):
- With cannon base damage 1, a lone pirate needs HP <= 3 to be beatable without
  any merge.
- Two pirates in the same column on consecutive rows block each other's shots.
- Merge budget roughly scales with number of rows minus ~5.
